**Root cause:** the dossier was never actually written to storage, but the app told you it had been. The brief's attachments and probes lists come straight from the form's live state, and in Qwik that state is a special wrapped object (a Proxy). The browser's local database (IndexedDB) refuses to store those and throws an error. `saveBriefToIdb` in `src/utils/idb.ts` caught that error and ignored it. So the "filed" stamp appeared, you were sent to the editor, and there was no dossier for that project. For Twyne's "publish to PDS / sign in with Bluesky" feature. Reference impl: github.com/mozzius/standard.horse (Vite+React SPA, no backend; `@atproto/oauth-client-browser` + `@atproto/api`).

**Lexicons** (authoritative JSON: raw.githubusercontent.com/mozzius/standard.horse/main/lexicons/...):
- `site.standard.publication` (key tid) — required `url` (uri), `name` (≤500 graphemes). optional `icon` blob, `description`, `basicTheme`, `preferences.showInDiscover`.
- `site.standard.document` (key tid) — required `site` (publication at:// or url), `title`, `publishedAt` (datetime). optional `path` (leading slash), `description`, `textContent` (plaintext, no markdown), `coverImage` blob ≤1MB, `content` (open union — each entry needs `$type`), `tags`, `updatedAt`, `bskyPostRef`, `contributors[]`.
- Content via `at.markpub.markdown`: `{ $type:"at.markpub.markdown", text:{ $type:"at.markpub.text", markdown:"..." }, flavor:"gfm"|"commonmark" }`.

**Writing records:** `com.atproto.repo.createRecord` (server assigns TID rkey) first publish → store returned uri/rkey; `putRecord` with stored rkey to update. Blobs via `uploadBlob`.

**Browser OAuth** (`@atproto/oauth-client-browser`, persists session in IndexedDB):
- Dev/loopback: `new BrowserOAuthClient({ handleResolver:"https://bsky.social", clientMetadata: atprotoLoopbackClientMetadata(clientId) })` where `clientId = http://localhost?redirect_uri=<origin/>&scope=<SCOPE>`.
- Prod: `BrowserOAuthClient.load({ clientId: \`${origin}/oauth-client-metadata.json\`, handleResolver })`. client_id MUST equal the fetch URL; filename must end exactly `/oauth-client-metadata.json` (consent UI hides raw URL). Serve dynamically per-origin to cover preview deploys.
- SCOPE = `"atproto blob:image/* include:site.standard.authFull"`. Reads are public (no scope); authFull grants repo access to standard.site collections; atproto+blob stay explicit.
- All `@atproto/*` is browser-only → must be dynamically `import()`ed client-side in Qwik (SSR eval would crash, like [[ai-sdk-oidc-browser-crash]]).

# Twyne pricing: new subscriptions

The new plan is `twyne_pro_v2`: USD 29/month before tax, with USD 10 in monthly retail Not Organic service credit. Unused included credit rolls over for one billing cycle. Top-ups are optional. Custom training and hosted voice are not part of this plan. BYOK and supported local writing remain available without this subscription.

The previous USD 12 checkout is no longer the entry point for new sales. Existing legacy subscriptions, webhook handling, prices and entitlements are unchanged. The new plan is a hosted editorial AI wallet plan; it does not grant legacy-only voice, research, collaboration or priority features.

## Activation

New checkout is disabled by default. Before enabling:

1. Deploy and map the provider plan `twyne_pro_v2` to the USD 29 monthly payment price and USD 10 grant; verify payment webhook and renewal/rollover behavior.
2. Deploy the Not Organic `/v1/wallet` product-scoped `subscriptions` summary, which supplies plan, product, status and billing period timestamps in milliseconds.
3. Verify linked account access, server-held assertion signing and `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true` inference with actual wallet debits. Missing identity or token exchange errors must stop the hosted path instead of spending legacy server-provider funds.
4. Set server `NOTORGANIC_TWYNE_PRO_V2_ENABLED=true` and build frontend with `PUBLIC_NOTORGANIC_TWYNE_PRO_V2_ENABLED=true`. Both gates must be enabled; unmapped provider checkout still rejects the purchase.
5. Verify signed-in checkout and confirmed wallet status. A return URL never grants paid status. Check BYOK/local and existing legacy subscribers separately.

New subscription UI intentionally excludes legacy-only feature promises. Payment provider configuration and real purchase verification are deployment boundaries, not inferred from source tests.

Free accounts can buy `twyne_credit_10`, `twyne_credit_25` or `twyne_credit_50` through the same authenticated checkout action using `pack_id`, independently of Pro. No recurring payment or premium entitlement is created. Hosted editorial requests already use the linked account wallet without a Pro check; legacy voice, research and collaboration gates are unchanged.

Credit packs use the existing server `NOTORGANIC_ENABLED=true` gate, independently of the Pro subscription flags. # Typst-native editor — brief plan

Status: proposal. Nothing built.

## What "Typst-native" should mean

The writer keeps writing in the page-view editor they have now. What changes is the document's source of truth:
it becomes a Typst document instead of HTML, and Typst sets the pages. The writer should never have to see
markup unless they open a source view.

The default is **not** a code editor for Typst. The text-first mode is an opt-in view of the same document.

## What it touches (measured 2026-09-23)

| Area | Today | Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Editor schema | Tiptap/ProseMirror, 33 extensions under `src/components/editor/extensions` | 33 |
| Storage | `folio-content.html` in IDB; `html: v.string()` in `convex/schema.ts` | ~25 read/write `.html` |
| Pagination | our own measurement engine (`__twynePagination`) | 15 |
| Export | DOCX (`exchange-docx`), PDF/print, markdown | 3 + 7 + 5 |
| Publishing | `htmlToMarkdown`/`stripHtml` → standard.site, micropub, blog | 5 |
| AI | prompts, personas, editorial notes all read manuscript HTML/text | many — read-only |

Rewriting the editor would touch most of the app. A bridge does not have to.

## Recommended shape: bridge, don't replace

1. **ProseMirror ↔ Typst serializer (both directions)** for the schema we already have: paragraphs, headings,
   marks, lists, quotes, notes, drop cap, and page layout settings. HTML stays the storage format in phase 1.
2. **Typst as the typesetter.** Compile with the typst WASM build (typst.ts) in a worker.
   - Use it for PDF export and a "proof" pane first.
   - Our measurement pagination stays for live editing until the proof matches it.
3. **Source view.** A CodeMirror pane with the Typst source of the current folio. Edits round-trip through the
   serializer. Anything the serializer can't represent is kept as an opaque "raw Typst" node, so it is never
   lost.
4. **Flip the source of truth** (only if 1–3 prove out).
   - Store `.typ` alongside HTML; add a `format` field to folio content and to the Convex schema.
   - Migrate lazily when a folio is opened.
   - Publishing and AI keep reading derived HTML/markdown.
5. **Retire the measurement pagination** once Typst proof and live view agree on page breaks.

## Risks

- WASM bundle size (typst.ts is several MB). Lazy-load it, and ship it inside the desktop app.
- Fonts: Typst needs the actual font files. We already commit Libre Baskerville cuts for OG cards, so reuse them.
- Round-trip fidelity. Collaborative edits and AI suggestions operate on ProseMirror steps. Typst is the output,
  not the editing model, until phase 4.
- Two paginators disagreeing during the transition. Label the Typst one "proof".

## First slice (about a week)

Serializer for the current schema + a "Export → PDF (Typst)" menu item + round-trip unit tests on the e2e
fixtures. That shows whether fidelity is achievable before anything else commits.

# Local & shipped models — brief plan

Status: proposal. Measurements come from Keating's on-device ledger
(`~/Projects/keating/scripts/on-device-site`).

## Models

| Model | Size | Where it runs | Job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `minishlab/potion-retrieval-32M` (ONNX) | ~131 MB, 512-d, ~4 ms/batch in Keating | **Desktop (bundled)** | Retrieval over folios, notes, apparatus, references |
| `minishlab/potion-multilingual-128m-onnx` | ~547 MB (model 512 MB + 35 MB tokenizer) | **Convex / server, on request**; optional desktop download | Multilingual retrieval, matching the multilingual replies |
| KEV-0.8B (the local Jev) | 0.8B params | **Desktop (bundled or first-run download)** via the existing `desktop/litert-server.ts` | Offline editorial review / notes |

Static (potion) embeddings are a lookup plus a mean, with no transformer at inference time. That is why the 32M
model is cheap enough to ship. The multilingual model is too heavy for the browser, which is why the web
calls the server for it.

## Routing

- **Desktop:** potion-32M and KEV run locally. The multilingual model is used when installed, otherwise the
  server.
- **Browser:** embeddings come from the server (multilingual). Twyne does not download 500 MB into a tab.
- **Server:** multilingual embedding as an action. Convex actions have runtime/memory limits, so it likely needs a
  small sidecar (the Railway service) that Convex calls. Verify before committing to an in-Convex ONNX runtime.
  Store vectors with a Convex `vectorIndex`.
- Keep one `EmbeddingProvider` interface (`embed(texts) → Float32Array[]`, `dimensions`, `modelId`).
  - Never mix vectors from different models in one index.
  - Key the index by `modelId`.

## Offline is degraded — say so

- Add a single "Offline mode" notice in settings and in the editor status area. It lists what changes:
  - KEV notes are shorter and less reliable than hosted Jev.
  - Search is literal-strong but weaker on paraphrase. Keating: potion-32M paraphrase MRR ≈ 0.55 vs literal 1.0.
  - Research/web features are unavailable.
- Tag every output that came from a local model, so a writer can tell offline quality apart from hosted quality.

## Paid trained models (separate from Pro)

`docs/pricing-rollout.md` already keeps custom training out of `twyne_pro_v2`, so this is a separate product:

- **Fine-tuned potion** distilled on the writer's own corpus: better paraphrase search on their material.
- **Fine-tuned KEV** on house style / editorial rubric: offline notes that sound like their editor.
- Billed per training run plus delivery. Delivery means a downloadable desktop model, or hosted.

## Waitlist + survey

- A waitlist form on the pricing page ("Trained models — join the waitlist") that stores email, plan, and one
  optional line about what they write.
  - Use a Convex table `waitlist` with the fields: `email`, `userId?`, `source`, `createdAt`, `surveySentAt?`.
- Later: send a short survey (corpus size, languages, desktop vs hosted, price anchor) to the list in one batch.
  Record `surveySentAt` so nobody is asked twice.
- Gate the form behind a feature flag, like the other pricing gates.

## Order

1. `EmbeddingProvider` + potion-32M in desktop + offline notice.
2. Server multilingual endpoint + vector index.
3. Ship KEV through `litert-server`.
4. Waitlist table + form. The survey is sent when there is something to price.

# Not Organic signup deployment — 2026-09-06

The PDS, portal server, and public identity frontend deployed successfully:

| Service | Deployment |
| --- | --- |
| PDS | `593e565a-0bb0-4f4d-be2a-079196becef9` |
| Portal | `7ee71b97-f12c-4758-ba3e-67dd34d084ef` |
| Landing / identity frontend | `47907b76-0168-45bf-aaa9-0dea0d6b4dad` |

PDS signing and admin secrets were generated directly into Railway and existing
secrets were preserved. Registration is configured without invites, with handles
under `.pds.notorganic.info`. The existing `/pds` persistent volume is retained.

Private bucket `notorganic-pds` in Railway's `iad` region supplies blob storage
and account-database backups. Credentials are server-held. An empty disposable
object passed PUT/GET/DELETE (200/200/204), and Litestream logged its first
account-database snapshot upload. This does not prove a full disaster recovery
of every PDS database and actor repository. The old R2 endpoint failed TLS;
its credential values were not printed or copied into source.

The public identity frontend serves the Create account action. Session checks
return 401 when signed out, and OAuth metadata and public JWKS return 200.
The initial signup check returned the expected 503 before PDS DNS was
configured. No real account creation or SMTP delivery is claimed.

## DNS configuration

These records were added to Porkbun using Sesame with credentials loaded
directly from Skate. Existing unrelated DNS records were preserved:

| Type | Host | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CNAME | `pds` | `4uty3sp7.up.railway.app` |
| CNAME | `*.pds` | `otyc38dm.up.railway.app` |
| CNAME | `_acme-challenge.pds` | `otyc38dm.authorize.railwaydns.net` |
| TXT | `_railway-verify.pds` | `railway-verify=db82d27f50380b411870e94b3d2145420605c2a4038c78861f81add31f315451` |

The TXT value is a public domain-ownership verification token. Recheck required
values with `railway domain status` before changing records if a domain has
since been removed or recreated. Railway confirmed the CNAME records had
propagated, and Google's public resolver returned the ownership TXT record.
Certificate issuance was still pending at that check.

## Remaining email and end-to-end verification

Use **Resend** for SMTP, as requested. Set `PDS_EMAIL_SMTP_URL` to a secure SMTP
URL using `smtp.resend.com:465`, username `resend`, and the URL-encoded Resend
API key as its password. Set `PDS_EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS` to an address on a domain
verified in Resend. Do not put SMTP passwords in chat or source control.
Redeploy the existing PDS image after changing these settings, preserving the
volume and generated identity keys.

An internal Railway SSH check returned 200 for PDS health (version 0.4.219),
server description (`inviteCodeRequired: false`, domain `.pds.notorganic.info`),
and OAuth metadata (issuer `https://pds.notorganic.info`). These checks do not
substitute for public DNS/TLS and a completed registration.

Then follow the account signup verification steps in `infra/runbook.md`, using
a fresh browser session and a controlled test email address. Porkbun access was
subsequently recovered through Skate; no Resend key was found in Skate, and the
configured OpenBao credential cannot list secret metadata. An authenticated
browser was unavailable, so no browser signup was performed. The external Vet
review remains unapproved and was not retried.

The goal is to make Twyne work the way Keating does:
- one Not Organic account (a DID, usually on `pds.notorganic.info`) is the writer's identity;
- wallet, inference, publishing and synced data all hang off that account.

## 1. How sign-in works today

Twyne has **three independent identity systems**:

| # | Path | Where | What it creates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | **better-auth**: email OTP (Resend) + passkeys | `convex/auth.ts`, `convex/auth.config.ts`, `src/utils/auth-client.ts`, `src/components/auth/auth-panel.tsx` | The Convex user. **All server data** (folios sync, comments, published pieces, profiles, subscriptions) is keyed to it. |
| B | **Bluesky / ATProto OAuth** | `src/utils/atproto.ts`, `/oauth-client-metadata.json`, `auth-panel.tsx` "Bluesky or PDS identity" | A *browser-only* session, `auth.value.provider === "atproto"`. No Convex user, so Twyne-hosted publish is unavailable. Used for PDS publishing. |
| C | **Not Organic link** (PKCE, `wallet:read`) | `src/utils/notorganic-connect.ts`, `src/components/settings/notorganic-connection.tsx`, `convex/providerIdentity.ts`, `convex/lib/notorganic.ts`, `convex/lib/providerLink.ts` | Not a sign-in. It **links** a DID to an existing better-auth user (`saveVerifiedLink`). Server then signs product assertions → `/v1/auth/token/exchange` for wallet and inference. |

`src/utils/auth-context.tsx` switches between `provider: "convex"` (A) and `provider: "atproto"` (B).
`linkDidFromLegacyBrowserSession` is the bridge from an old B session to a DID link.

## 2. How Keating does it (target)

- **Sign-in:** `id.notorganic.info/authorize` with PKCE → `POST api.notorganic.info/v1/public/token`.
  - The response is a 300-second DPoP-bound capability whose `sub` is the account DID.
  - `device_session: true` adds a rotating refresh token (`/v1/public/device/token`, revoke via
    `/v1/public/device/revoke`).
  - The DPoP key is a non-extractable WebCrypto key.
- **Identity:** `GET /v1/account` (any scope) with the capability.
- **Data:** local-first.
  - Encrypted sync; the key comes from `GET /v1/sync/account-key` (scope `sync:key:read`).
  - Transport is Gun P2P.
  - No Keating-owned user table.
- **Publishing:** the same DID's repo on the PDS (standard.site).
- `https://twyne.love` is **already an approved public client** for product `twyne` in the gateway
  (`apps/gateway/src/public-client-product.ts`).

## 3. Creem (payments) — where it still is

New sales already go through Not Organic (`createNotOrganicCheckout` in `src/routes/pricing/index.tsx`,
credit packs in `convex/lib/providerCheckout.ts`). Creem remains **only for legacy subscribers**:

| Kind | Files |

| Live server path | `convex/http.ts` (webhook), `convex/payments.ts` (`createCheckout` — no UI caller left; `getMySubscription`, `applyCreemEvent`), `convex/lib/creem.ts`, `convex/lib/entitlement.ts` (`CREEM_PRO_PRODUCT_IDS`), `convex/schema.ts` (subscriptions table), `convex/profiles.ts`, `convex/lib/rateLimit.ts` |

| Config | `.env.example` (12 lines), `package.json` `test:creem*`, `playwright.config.ts` |

| Docs | `docs/architecture/data-and-sync.md`, `docs/my-desk-usage-profile-spec.md` |

**Safe to remove now:**
- `payments.createCheckout` and its rate-limit bucket;
- the Creem checkout e2e setup.

**Keep until the last legacy subscription ends:**
- the webhook;
- the subscriptions table;
- the entitlement lookup.

## 4. Plan

Convex stays the data store. Its customJwt verifier doesn't cover the gateway's EdDSA, DPoP-bound tokens, so
Not Organic is bridged into better-auth rather than replacing it.

1. **Not Organic as the sign-in** (single button: "Continue with Not Organic").
   - Browser PKCE + DPoP against `id.notorganic.info`, with `device_session: true`.
     Reuse `notorganic-connect.ts` and the Keating `oauth.ts` flow.
   - Browser sends `{access_token, dpop_proof for GET /v1/account}` to a new better-auth endpoint
     (`/api/auth/sign-in/notorganic`).
   - That endpoint calls `/v1/account`, gets the DID, and finds or creates the user through the existing
     `providerIdentity` DID link. It then issues the normal better-auth session, so every Convex query keeps
     working unchanged.
   - Scopes: `wallet:read infer:* sync:key:read`, requested once.
2. **Existing accounts.**
   - Email/passkey users sign in the old way once. The existing link flow attaches their DID, and after that
     Not Organic is their sign-in.
   - Keep email OTP as a hidden "recover old account" path until linked accounts dominate.
3. **Collapse ATProto into the same identity.** The DID from step 1 *is* the writer's PDS repo, so:
   - PDS publishing uses that account;
   - it requests ATProto OAuth against its PDS only when writing records;
   - the separate "Bluesky session" mode and the `provider: "atproto"` split in `auth-context.tsx` go away.
   - Third-party Bluesky PDS accounts remain a "publish elsewhere" option, not an identity.
4. **Data, native like Keating.**
   - Local-first IDB stays primary; Convex sync is keyed by DID-linked user.
   - Optional later: encrypt synced folio content with the `/v1/sync/account-key` key, so the server holds
     ciphertext, as in Keating.
5. **Creem retirement.** Remove `createCheckout` now; the webhook and table stay until the last legacy
   subscription lapses.

- The gateway must allow CORS from `https://twyne.love` for `/v1/public/token` and `/v1/account`.
  - `twyne.love` is registered as a client; CORS is not verified yet.
  - Desktop needs a loopback callback, like Keating's `CORS_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`.
- The capability lives 300 s. Server-side work (wallet, inference) keeps using the existing product-assertion

- Existing users with Creem subscriptions must keep their entitlement after switching to a Not Organic sign-in.
  - Entitlement follows the Convex user, and step 2 keeps the same user, so this holds only if the linking
    happens *before* the first Not Organic-only sign-in.

   - The JWT `sub` = better-auth user id, so `identity.subject` = user id.

# Not Organic–native sign-in and data

Status: implemented 2026-09-23. Creem, email OTP, passkeys and Bluesky-as-identity are removed.

Twyne now works the way Keating does: one Not Organic account (a DID, usually on `pds.notorganic.info`) is the
writer's identity. Their wallet, plan, inference and synced data all hang off that account.

## How sign-in works

1. **Browser** (`src/utils/notorganic-connect.ts`, `startNotOrganicSignIn`): PKCE against
   `id.notorganic.info/authorize`.
   - `client_id` = the page origin.
   - `redirect_uri` = `${origin}/auth/notorganic/`.
   - `scope` = `wallet:read`, `product` = `twyne`.
   - The attempt (state, verifier, returnTo) lives in sessionStorage.
2. **Callback page** (`src/routes/auth/notorganic/`): posts `{code, verifier, origin}` to the Better Auth
   endpoint `POST /api/auth/sign-in/notorganic`.
3. **Server** (`convex/lib/notorganicSignIn.ts`, wired in `convex/auth.ts`):
   - checks that `origin` is in `trustedOrigins`;
   - redeems the code server-side (`redeemProviderLink`), so there is no gateway CORS and no caller-supplied
     DID.
4. **Mapping the DID to a user:** the verified DID becomes a Better Auth `account` row with
   `providerId: "notorganic"`, `accountId: <did>`.
   - New users get a user row with an undeliverable placeholder email: `<sha256(did)[:16]>@notorganic.invalid`.
     The UI hides it.
   - The display name is the Not Organic handle, refreshed on each sign-in.
5. **Session and DID link:** `onSignedIn` writes the `providerIdentities` link (`saveVerifiedLink`), and a normal
   Better Auth session is issued (crossDomain cookie). Convex auth is unchanged:
   - `identity.subject` = Better Auth user id;
   - `tokenIdentifier` = `${CONVEX_SITE_URL}|${userId}`.

Server-side wallet/inference calls still use the product-assertion exchange keyed by the linked DID
(`convex/lib/notorganic.ts`).

## Entitlement

`convex/lib/entitlement.ts` `userIsPro` reads the Not Organic wallet and applies `hasCurrentTwynePlan`
(`src/utils/subscription-plan.ts`). The pricing page reads the same wallet. There is no local subscriptions
table.

## ATProto / Bluesky

ATProto is a **publishing connection**, not an identity:
- The Share dialog's "Your own repo" section has a handle field and a "Connect PDS" button that start ATProto
  OAuth.
- `/auth/callback/` restores that publishing session (`auth.value.atproto`).
- `auth.value.provider` is always `"convex"`.

## Legacy accounts

Email/passkey accounts were deprecated with no migration path; nobody held a Creem subscription. The tooling is
in `convex/legacyAccounts.ts` (all functions internal):

```sh
npx convex run legacyAccounts:sendDeprecationNotices '{"dryRun":true}'
npx convex run legacyAccounts:sendDeprecationNotices '{"dryRun":false}'
npx convex run legacyAccounts:retireLegacyAccounts '{"dryRun":true}'
npx convex run legacyAccounts:retireLegacyAccounts '{"dryRun":false}'
```

- Add `--prod` to target production.
- Notices are recorded in `legacyAccountNotices`, so re-running never emails anyone twice.
- Retirement reuses the account-deletion job (`scheduleAccountDeletion`), which purges synced data and the
  Better Auth user.

## Open items

- The gateway maps `https://twyne.love` as a public client for product `twyne`. `www.twyne.love` and the desktop
  loopback origin need their own registration, otherwise sign-in from them is rejected at `/authorize`.
- Optional, as in Keating: encrypt synced folio content with `/v1/sync/account-key` so the server holds
  ciphertext.
- PDS publishing on `pds.notorganic.info` depends on the scope fallback noted in `publishing-from-twyne.md`.

Typecheck and lint pass, and every unit test file passes when run on its own. I haven't run the e2e suite or tried a real Not Organic sign-in in a browser.

**What changed**
- **Sign-in:** the sign-in panel now has a single "Continue with Not Organic" button. The server redeems the sign-in code, links the account to a Twyne user and starts a normal session, so the rest of the app works as before.
- **Paid plans:** the pricing page and every Pro check read the Not Organic wallet. The Creem code, its webhook and its tables are removed.
- **Bluesky:** it's now only a publishing connection. File → Share → "Your own repo" has a handle field and a **Connect PDS** button, and `/auth/callback/` now says "PDS connected".
- **Removed:**
  - The old "connect Not Organic" card in Settings.
  - The passkey package.
  - The Creem config lines and test scripts.
  - Two e2e tests that relied on email codes: `journey` and `collaboration`.
- **Copy and docs:** the sign-in page, FAQ, privacy and terms pages are updated. So are `notorganic-native-identity.md` (now marked implemented, with the retirement commands), `publishing-from-twyne.md` and the architecture diagram.
- **Unplanned fix:** `convex/agentPrompts.ts` now starts with `"use node";`. Without it the Convex push failed on `import.meta`, which came from your uncommitted prompt changes.

**Needs your go-ahead.** My permissions blocked reading production data, so I stopped before anything touching prod. In order:

1. **Check prod before deploying.** Look at the `subscriptions`, `webhookEvents` and `e2eOtps` tables in prod. If any still hold rows, the deploy may be rejected, because those tables are no longer in the schema.
2. **Deploy:** `npx convex deploy`, then push the frontend to Railway.

4. **Send it:** run the same command with `'{"dryRun":false}'`. Each send is recorded, so re-running never emails anyone twice.
5. **Back up, then delete:** take a snapshot (`npx convex export --prod`), then run `legacyAccounts:retireLegacyAccounts` in the same way, dry run first. This deletes each old account and its synced data.
